lots.guide_summary: All six surviving entries are SOLD Gowans hammers for single pairs of 9ct gold cufflinks, $160 to $400 (2.3g to 6.4g, roughly $49 to $70 per gram), Oct 2025 to May 2026. No unsold or asking entries. This lot is TWO pairs, so on Gowans form the pair-for-pair value is roughly $320 to $800 hammer depending on weight, which is not stated. AUD, no conversion.
lots.working: Lowest same-kind SOLD is $160 per pair (2.3g, damaged); lowest undamaged pair $180 (3.7g). Two pairs at the lowest: 2 x $160 = $320. keep_max_hammer = 320 / 1.22 = 262.30, round down to $260 hammer ($317 all-in). flip: likely resale from the SOLD run for 3.6g to 3.7g pairs, about $220 a pair (results $180 and $220), so 2 x $220 = $440 hammer; less about 15% seller commission and fees ($66) and $0 postage (resell in a Tasmanian room) = $374; flip_max_hammer = 374 / 2.44 = 153.3, round down to $150. If Armitage gives a weight, re-price at about $50 per gram hammer (lowest per-gram SOLD, $49/g) for the keep ceiling: e.g. 10g x $49 = $490, / 1.22 = $400.
lots.confidence_reason: 9ct stamp clearly read on the rectangular pair and '9ct' plus a second word (possibly a maker or 'APEX'-type mark) on the shield pair; six matching Gowans SOLD results opened. Held at Medium because the weight is not stated and drives the price.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped 375269 (timber box of badges including a pair of 9ct cufflinks, $260): mixed lot, cannot isolate the cufflinks. Searched Gowans for 9ct cufflinks again: 402955 (15ct and opal pair, 14.3g, $1000) is a different metal and kind, not used.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged photo 2: rectangular pair stamped '9ct' (clear on one, partly struck on the other); shield pair stamped '9ct' followed by a short word or maker mark, partly legible. All four links have chains intact and ball ends present. Engraved monograms on the shields, rubbed.
lots.condition: Light wear, engraving and monograms rubbed, no obvious breaks; chains and ball ends present. Weight unknown.
lots.question_for_armitage: What is the total weight in grams of the two pairs, and can you confirm the shield pair is stamped 9ct (and what the second mark reads)? Any repairs, solder or base-metal chains?
